head_text:
# Astra UI

Astra UI is Daeron's private Android command center for local coding agents. Built with Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86, Expo Router, and TypeScript, it provides a mobile-first control surface where each rig runs its own local backend and the phone streams telemetry, inspects diffs, resolves execution approvals, and edits per-agent configuration. Nothing is published to an app store or routed through a cloud backend.

First-class active providers in this build are **Factory Droid** and **Codex**. **OpenCode**, **Google AntiGravity**, and **DeepSeek Harness** are registered in the provider catalog as planned targets for subsequent integration passes.

## Quickstart

Install Node.js LTS on the host machine and Expo Go (SDK 57 compatible) on your Android device. Run in the repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npx expo start
```

Keep the workstation and Android phone on the same Wi-Fi network, then scan the Metro QR code in Expo Go. If the installed Expo Go build does not match SDK 57, install the matching version from <https://expo.dev/go> or build the standalone preview APK below.

For a local desktop browser preview:

```sh
npm run web
```

Fonts (`Inter`, `JetBrains Mono`, `Space Grotesk`) are bundled as local assets and loaded by `src/app/_layout.tsx`. No agent daemon is required to run the demo scaffold.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Install locked dependencies |
| `npx expo start` | Start the Metro development server |
| `npm run web` | Start the web preview in a desktop browser |
| `npm run typecheck` | Run `tsc --noEmit` static type verification |
| `npx expo lint` | Run Expo lint checks |
| `npx expo install --fix` | Align package versions with Expo SDK 57 |
| `npx expo-doctor` | Diagnose Expo config and dependency health |
| `npm run export` | Export the static web bundle (`expo export --platform web`) |

## Architecture & File Responsibility

Navigation is managed by **Expo Router** under `src/app/`. Non-route modules live under `src/theme/`, `src/components/`, `src/providers/`, `src/transport/`, and `src/state/`.

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/app/_layout.tsx` | Root Expo Router layout; loads bundled fonts and mounts state/theme providers |
| `src/app/index.tsx` | Command deck: rig selector strip, telemetry summary, active and planned provider cards |
| `src/app/agent/[provider]/index.tsx` | Provider workspace: sessions list, quick actions, model/mode overview, rig context |
| `src/app/agent/[provider]/session/[sid].tsx` | Live session stream view and bottom command/prompt composer |
| `src/app/agent/[provider]/settings.tsx` | Schema-generated per-agent configuration editor |
| `src/app/agent/[provider]/changes.tsx` | Working-tree diff inspection per provider |
| `src/app/approvals.tsx` | Cross-agent execution approval inbox |
| `src/app/machines/[id].tsx` | Machine detail view, rig telemetry, and LAN endpoint address editor |
| `src/theme/tokens.ts` | Frozen Somnus visual contract: obsidian palette, glass hierarchy, typography scale, spacing, radii, motion |
| `src/components/ui/` | Core primitives: `Shell`, `GlassPanel`, `Button`, `Chip`, `StatusDot`, `SectionHeader`, `Sheet`, `ListRow`, `Metric`, `CodeBlock`, `Icon` |
| `src/components/agent/` | Domain components: `ProviderCard`, `StreamView`, `Composer`, `ApprovalCard`, `DiffCard` |
| `src/providers/registry.ts` | Provider registry and configuration schemas (Droid and Codex active; OpenCode, AntiGravity, DeepSeek Harness planned) |
| `src/transport/types.ts` | `AgentTransport` interface contract for sessions, streams, approvals, diffs, and machine metrics |
| `src/transport/demo.ts` | `DemoTransport` deterministic local fixtures implementing `AgentTransport` |
| `src/state/agent-store.tsx` | React context + `AsyncStorage` persistence (`astra.rig-addresses.v2` and `astra.agent-settings.v1`) |
| `docs/FACTORY.md` | Visual contract, architecture specification, demo boundaries, and LAN integration rules |
| `docs/VALIDATION.md` | Verification gate checklist and current execution status |

## Demo Boundaries

- **Persisted state:** Only machine LAN addresses (`astra.rig-addresses.v2`) and per-agent configuration settings (`astra.agent-settings.v1`) persist across restarts via `AsyncStorage`.
- **Fixture state:** Sessions, token streams, working-tree diffs, pending approvals, and rig hardware metrics are served in-memory by `DemoTransport` (`src/transport/demo.ts`). Interactive actions (sending prompts, resolving approvals, toggling settings, editing machine endpoints) mutate state within the running session, and persisted keys survive reload.
- **Zero external network calls:** No socket or HTTP connection is opened to a rig in this scaffold. There is no cloud relay, no automatic LAN discovery service, and no synchronized external database.

## Standalone Android APK (EAS Preview)

`eas.json` defines an internal `preview` profile configured to output a directly installable Android `.apk` (`"buildType": "apk"`). To build with an Expo account:

```sh
npx eas-cli@latest login
npx eas-cli@latest build:configure
npx eas-cli@latest build --platform android --profile preview
```

Download the artifact from the EAS build URL and install it directly on the target Android device (e.g., Galaxy S24 Ultra). Reference: <https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/apk/>.

# Astra UI

A private, native-feeling agent workspace. Expo + React Native + TypeScript. Shared StyleSheet tokens; no Tailwind compiler, synchronization backend, or discovery service. This is Daerons personal highly customized, mobile application + mcp-server/plugin so that he may install the plugin to opencode, factory-droid-cli, maybe even codex, and all other coding agents, he will install as .apk on his phone, while the device will spin up a server locally. This is not a publishable app, but that is exactly why daeron wants it to be the single greatest command center of all time for his coding agents. The current color scheming is atrocius and must follow the Somnus-Design-System but modernized. The app must look like a 5 billion dollar app that nobody ever will see.

## Run on your Android phone

Install Node.js LTS on your computer and Expo Go on your phone. Extract this folder. Open a terminal in this folder, then run these commands one at a time:

```sh
npm ci
```

```sh
npx expo start
```

Keep your computer and phone on the same Wi-Fi. Open Expo Go and scan the QR code printed by Expo. This scaffold uses Expo SDK 57 from the current blank TypeScript template; use a matching Expo Go version. If your installed Expo Go does not support this SDK, obtain its compatible Android build from https://expo.dev/go, or use the preview APK route below.

For a desktop browser preview:

```sh
npm run web
```

This demo needs no agent server. Fonts are packaged as assets, not fetched by the running UI. Development mode still needs the Metro server; a built preview APK bundles the app for standalone use.

## Try the demo

- Tap an OpenCode or Droid card to open that provider's workspace.
- Tap the Astra wordmark on a phone to open provider-grouped navigation. At 900px and above, the same navigation becomes a persistent sidebar.
- Tap a machine tile to switch its context; tap its ellipsis to edit the saved server address.
- Open provider controls with the sliders icon. Model profile and Build/Plan mode belong to the selected provider on the selected machine.
- Expand the terminal, type `/`, select a suggestion, and send it. `/help`, `/status`, and `/clear` work locally. OpenCode also has `/review`; Droid has `/logs`.
- Open the working tree for an illustrative change preview.
- Return to a provider/machine during the same app session to find its current demo output and controls intact.

**Only machine addresses persist across app restarts.** Sessions and controls are in-memory UI state. The screen is explicitly labeled LOCAL DEMO. Metrics, model profiles, commands, sessions, and changes are fixtures. No command is executed and no server connection is made. Demo command names do not assert that the real agents support the same names.

## Android APK

The included `eas.json` has an internal preview profile that produces an installable APK. It is not an app-store release. With an Expo account, run each command separately:

```sh
npx eas-cli@latest login
```

```sh
npx eas-cli@latest build:configure
```

```sh
npx eas-cli@latest build --platform android --profile preview
```

Download and install the resulting APK on your Android device. EAS may ask to create a project and signing credentials. No APK was built as part of this handoff. A local Android build remains possible with an Android SDK/JDK installation; it is not required to preview the UI.

Official build reference: https://docs.expo.dev/build-reference/apk/

## Files

| File | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `App.tsx` | Screen composition, local interaction state, saved addresses, demo commands |
| `src/theme.ts` | Palette, syntax roles, font families, spacing, radii, motion |
| `src/styles.ts` | Workspace layout and shared screen styling |
| `src/data.ts` | Typed demo fixtures and per-provider command menus |
| `src/components/DeviceStrip.tsx` | Horizontal machine selection and address actions |
| `src/components/AgentPanel.tsx` | Provider entry cards |
| `src/components/TerminalDrawer.tsx` | Animated terminal, input, completion menu |
| `src/components/Sheet.tsx` | Address, provider-controls, navigation, and change panels |
| `src/components/Primitives.tsx` | Icons, buttons, indicators, section headings |
| `docs/FACTORY.md` | Visual rules and exact extension boundaries |

## Validation

```sh
npm run typecheck
```

```sh
npx expo install --check
```

```sh
npm run export
```

See `docs/VALIDATION.md` for checks actually performed on this handoff.
